Bülow MDEA reproduction: second pressure-gap diagnosis

No single convention explains the discrepancy

Seven expressible one-factor probes retain 63 qualified states out of the 67-row primary inventory. Rows 11, 18, 50 and 51 were not retried, by owner instruction. None brings the five complete isotherms into their frozen SI S3 ±3 percentage-point windows. Evidence type: numerical diagnosis. The primary reproduction remains inconclusive. No parameter, primary method, interpretation or manuscript was changed. Independent delivered scientific review remains open; manuscript use is not promoted.

At high temperature and loading below 0.5, replacing σ³ by d³ in association strength raises pressure by only about 2%. Other probes either lower it or have negligible effect. This is too small to explain the deficit. All temperatures below refer to nominal isotherm labels; calculations retain each source row’s actual temperature and molalities on 1 kg initial water.

Corrected Figure 4

The first diagnosis followed an orange experimental marker at loading ≈0.499, reporting 4.50 bar. That value and its 39% deficit are withdrawn by the round-1 review. The corrected model stroke is near pixel y=195, giving 3.79 bar. At source row 20 (373.14 K, loading 0.499154), our total pressure is 2.726 bar and our CO₂ partial pressure is 1.753 bar: respectively 28.1% and 53.8% below the corrected model line.

Figure 4 (p.6332) plots 19 wt% MDEA at 313, 333, 373 and 393 K. These are the only Kuranov CO₂ curves in the paper and SI: SI S3 supplies eight deviations, while SI figures concern sulfolane properties and the calculation flowchart. There is no plotted 32.3 wt% model curve to extract. The caption and axis say CO₂ partial pressure, while the adjacent paragraph calls the predictions system pressures. This conflict remains unresolved; both of our observables are compared without relabeling either one.

Marker masking and uncertainty

Digitization code reads the original embedded raster xref 281 (500×364 pixels), never the earlier connected-component trace. Axis calibration: loading 0/1.5 at x=108/482; pressure 1/10 bar at y=281/133, logarithmic vertically. Each manually located experimental marker is masked with an 8-pixel-radius disk, including markers of the other series. Color and a broad center guide isolate model strokes. Masked gaps use linear interpolation only between retained line pixels; a local quadratic fit to the nearest 24 unmasked columns checks crossings. The guide restricts the search and is not an independent measurement.

The conservative vertical bound is ±5 pixels, a multiplicative pressure factor of 1.0809 (−7.48%, +8.09%). A separate ±1-pixel horizontal bound corresponds to ±0.00401 loading; the slope contribution is not included in the quoted vertical bound. At row 20 it contributes about another 2% in pressure, so even a conservative combined bound of about 11% cannot account for either deficit there. These are image-reading bounds, not confidence intervals or experimental uncertainties. The crossing checks in metadata are within this bound. The inspected overlay follows the prediction line through the old erroneous marker crossing; masked regions are magenta and the retained line is blue. Classification: review, because the source is a low-resolution raster and gaps are interpolated; the second interpolation check shares the same pixels.

Probe definitions and numerical limits

All probes use the immutable Engine main-d513820994a78bfe628d42fffd55b2eeab6f89bd wheel, SHA-256 ca7093ca721fdc80226c74d018a582f31705684c6995e80b0492c193334dd5d5, and the separate original .venv-bulow. No root dependency file changed. Each probe changes one physical convention, uses ../run.py for solving and qualification, and retains its original starts, solver defaults and budgets. Residual, balance, replay, positive-permittivity and positive pressure-slope checks are inherited unchanged. All seven probes qualify all 63 submitted rows. The four excluded rows remain unresolved, rather than being relabeled successes.

  1. Packing: evaluate Held 2014 Eq.22 with the printed ionic energies in Bülow Table 2. Held actually uses Eq.21 (0.88σ) for ions; this is the authorized diagnostic replacement, not a correction to the source. Only packing changes.
  2. Dispersion 2b: admit all ionic dispersion pairs, with zero unlike interaction coefficients where the primary same-sign exclusion made them unconsumed. Variant 2a is skipped: this wheel declares only all-ion-pairs or exclusion of every same-sign pair; no self-only exclusion or diagonal k_ii is admitted.
  3. Electrostatic diameters: use the same Eq.22 temperature-dependent diameter for both Debye–Hückel and Born, leaving packing at its primary 0.88σ.
  4. Association: multiply each resolved original strength’s volume by \([(d_i+d_j)/(σ_i+σ_j)]^3\). Original Wolbach–Sandler energies and mixing volumes are resolved before this multiplication; no packing diameter is changed.
  5. Cross association: remove the MDEA–CO₂ prohibition and add both donor–acceptor orientations with Wolbach–Sandler energies and volumes (Bülow Eqs.23/25).
  6. Reference pressure: declare 100000 Pa on every reaction’s reference; mixture pressure remains the solved bubble pressure.
  7. Hydronium: keep the proton identifier as an internal index, replace its element inventory by H₃O⁺ and its mass by 0.01902322 kg/mol, and subtract one water reactant per proton produced in each reaction. Thus water dissociation uses two waters; the other three reactions gain one water reactant. Printed ion parameters, reaction constants, activities and starts remain unchanged.
  8. No alternate run: Bülow Eq.26 explicitly defines Tref=298.15 K. Table 3 agrees with the primary polynomial: coefficients −0.118, −7.59×10⁻⁴ K⁻¹, −1.32×10⁻⁵ K⁻², +1.25×10⁻⁷ K⁻³. Temperature differences in kelvin give dimensionless k_ij. No ambiguity was found.

The wheel admits constant packing/Born/Debye–Hückel diameters but no temperature correlations for these families. For these isothermal solves we evaluate the specified diameter separately at each row’s actual T and declare that constant. The association strength conversion likewise resolves at each actual T. This preserves composition and density derivatives needed by the primary equilibrium solver; it does not qualify temperature derivatives or caloric properties. Probe code, per-probe example declarations and execution provenance retain this boundary. The 2b declaration initially lacked the newly consumed zero same-sign unlike coefficients and was rejected at admission; adding those zeros resolved the declaration without a solver or scientific-method change.

Sources, reproduction and remaining unknowns

Read sources: Bülow 2021 methods Eqs.12–26, Tables 1–3, results pp.6331–6333 and limitations; its complete SI (S1–S4, Figures S1–S3); Held 2014 §2 and Eqs.21–22. Exact Bülow equation and table forms were checked against the Zotero PDF. The Bülow and SI PDF hashes match ../sources.json; the Bülow and Held Markdown reading copies were compared to their shelf index and current Zotero companions. The shelf was read from the main checkout because it is absent in this worktree; no main-checkout file was written. The declared primary equations and data are reused, not re-estimated. No general claim about amine parameter transfer is made.

Unrecovered author dielectric inputs, exact implementation conventions, exact Table S3 row selections and scored pressure observable remain unknown. The four primary numerical failures remain with Engine issue 912. The results do not prove an error in the paper or Engine, recover the authors’ program, validate a physical model or establish process suitability. No interpretation change is recommended from these probes.
